newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU acts to protect electronic payment consumers.
newsitem.headline: EU acts to protect electronic payment consumers.

text.p: The European Commission issued recommendations on Wednesday intended to protect consumers who use electronic payment systems, warning that it would propose binding rules if they were not followed.
The text asks companies offering services such as cash-withdrawal, debit and charge cards or phone and online banking to implement various measures by the end of 1998.
EU Financial Services Commissioner Mario Monti said in a statement the move was needed to strengthen confidence in the new technologies, especially as the EU prepares to adopt a single currency.

The recommendations say companies should provide clear information to consumers about their fees, commissions, interest rates and reference foreign currency exchange rates and details about each transaction.

They say consumers should not be liable for more than 150 ecus ($166) if their cards are lost or stolen unless thay have acted with "extreme negligence" -- and should bear no liability once they have reported the loss.

Electronic payment operators should set up an around-the-clock system to allow consumers to report losses. They should also be liable for uncompleted, defective or unauthorised transactions, the recommendations say.

Consumers, meanwhile, should notify companies promptly of loss or thefts, unauthorised transactions or other irregularities and make efforts to keep their personal identification codes secrety, the recommendations say.
EU governments are asked to ensure that systems are set up by the end of 1998 to settle disputes between consumers and operators.

"We strongly believe that the industry will voluntarily give effect to these requirements," EU Consumer Commissioner Emma Bonino said in a statement. "If it will not be the case, we will propose a directive." -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
